task: Review the planned Prism hardening for provider dispatcher permissions, gate term matching, concern evidence verification, and prompt intent coverage.
user_intent: Norven asked Cap to process the risks found in the Prism implementation review instead of leaving them as status notes.
main_claim: The next implementation should make Prism safer as an opposition layer: provider review calls should not run with broad execution permissions, deterministic gate matching should avoid obvious substring false positives, concern acceptance should require stronger proof than file or command existence, and the current prompt wording should authorize implementation when the user says to process risks.
changed_reality: Planned: runtime/prism/bin/prism-dispatch will use safer provider command defaults and self-check them.
Planned: runtime/prism/bin/prism gate matching will stop treating substrings such as completeness as completion claims.
Planned: runtime/prism/bin/prism concern resolution evidence validation will require receipt-like executed checks for verification evidence.
Planned: runtime/core/prompt_intent.py will classify direct Chinese instructions such as 处理这些风险点 as implementation authority.

evidence.summary: Current dispatcher uses Kimi --quiet and Claude Code bypassPermissions for provider review calls.
Current gate matching uses substring checks, and concern resolution evidence only proves file or command existence.
Current classifier does not treat the user's current phrase 可以，请处理这些风险点 as implementation.

known_constraints: Do not weaken Stop hook anti-empty-work blocking or final completion claim checks.
Do not claim cross-host provider-call interception.
Do not expand providers beyond Kimi and Claude Code.
Do not use a provider review path that can mutate the repo while acting as Prism opposition.
Keep evidence structured enough that later checks can distinguish an executed check from a merely existing command name.
Avoid introducing a new brittle keyword maze while fixing the obvious substring false positives.
